IPv4 loopback convention (always 127.0.0.1, never localhost)
nodes.rationale: On Windows localhost resolves to ::1 (IPv6) and the Vite proxy fails with ECONNREFUSED ::1:5002, so every frontend-facing URL uses 127.0.0.1.

nodes.label: TOKEN_OPEN_STATUS = "active" / TOKEN_CLOSED_STATUS = "completed"
nodes.rationale: The 500 (errno 1265) came from writing the literal 'closed' into the tokens.status enum; the status literals and the enum were made to agree earlier (pre-acdb5d5) and are correct at HEAD 50867ac, so the defect is already fixed in the tree.

HAG-212 report: money integrity, duplicate bill payments
Revenue rule: sum bills.total, never bills.paid_amount
nodes.rationale: bills.paid_amount is written by settlePendingBill from paid_amount + due against a bill total that no longer exists, so summing it double-counts; it currently reads 3530 against an 80.00 real bill total. Every fixed aggregate instead sums bills.total.

nodes.label: De-dup rule: one payment row per bill, latest completed wins
nodes.rationale: payments carries exact duplicate rows per bill (41 rows, 40 redundant); applied as query-time filtering on payments.bill_id — MAX(id) per bill plus keeping rows with bill_id IS NULL; no row was ever physically deleted.

nodes.label: settlePendingBill (orphan payment-row bug)
nodes.rationale: settlePendingBill selects bills WHERE id = ? before computing due, so settling a bill deleted after the select inserts an orphan payment row — one of the two data bugs behind the duplicate mess.

nodes.label: asRows callback defect in src/config/db.js
nodes.rationale: mysql2's promise pool resolves every statement as a tuple ([rows/ResultSetHeader, fields]); db.js passes a callback asRows(result) that unwraps by Array.isArray(result[1]), so the callback form returns the header object for writes and the fields array for LIMIT-1 reads. Every callback caller was one level too shallow; fixing it repo-wide would change the contract for ~10000 raw await db.query calls, so it was left alone and accountsController now reads the tuple itself.

nodes.label: HAG-46 report: accounts schema drift (9 tables folded into schema-v4.sql)
schema-v4.sql (+171 lines, additive)
nodes.rationale: Makes schema-v4.sql sufficient on its own so the 9 accounts tables exist whether or not any model runs — a clean install of schema-v4.sql alone previously produced 72 of the live 130 tables, so the app schema only existed because models silently ran their ensureSchema() on the live db.

nodes.label: migrations/20261018_accounts_schema_drift.sql (additive, IF NOT EXISTS guarded)
nodes.rationale: Every statement is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS with no DROP/ALTER/MODIFY/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE, so re-running cannot remove or alter anything; idempotency proven by loading into scratch databases repeatedly.

nodes.label: AccountsExpansionModel.js (unwired DDL for 9 accounts tables)
nodes.rationale: Its ensureSchema() DDL defines purchase_orders, vendor_payment_records, petty_cash_entries, gst_return_records, profit_center_entries, account_bank_ledgers, payroll_records, payment_gateway_settings and bank_reconciliation_matches, but nothing in src/ calls it or requires it — it is dead DDL; app.js's ensureAccountsExpansionSchema alias silently ran the wrong model (TransactionsModel), which is why the drift was invisible.

nodes.label: ensureAccountsExpansionSchema alias (silently wrong)
nodes.rationale: app.js:34 imports ensureAccountsExpansionSchema from TransactionsModel, whose ensureSchema() creates only the transactions table; it returned success so no one noticed the 9 accounts tables were never provisioned — the correct alias is a two-line change owned by the accounts card, out of scope for this ticket.

nodes.label: accountsRoutes.js (50 routes, local ensureAccountsSchema ALTERs payments)
accounts_transactions table (unused by any route)
nodes.rationale: A 9th absence from schema-v4.sql defined in AccountsModel.js, not AccountsExpansionModel.js; 'accounts' as a table does not exist — the live v4 ledger is transactions + transaction_entries + chart_of_accounts.

nodes.label: 6 petty-cash/GST write routes return 501 by design
nodes.rationale: Petty cash and GST writes are intentionally refused: they are derived read-only views over the v4 payments and invoices tables; creating petty_cash_entries/gst_return_records tables would not fix the routes — the 501 is a deliberate code decision that pre-dates this ticket.

nodes.label: createUserRecordTx (two INSERTs on one pooled connection)
nodes.rationale: Both the users and employees INSERTs now run in one transaction on a single pooled connection, each header read via const [header] = await connection.query(...); any throw rolls back and returns 500 with the real error code; connection.release() in finally so failed requests no longer leak pooled connections; the {id: users.id, name} fallback is gone so a 201 always means both rows exist.

nodes.label: requireEmployeeRow (strict 404 when no employees row)
nodes.rationale: The old call site employeeId = (await resolveEmployee(employeeId)) || employeeId silently swallowed null and kept using the raw users.id, which became salary_payments.employee_id; createPayment now calls requireEmployeeRow so no employees row → 404 and no payment is written, while resolveEmployee keeps its contract for estimateSalary.

nodes.label: mysql2 pool tuple contract ([rows,fields] / [header,undefined])
nodes.rationale: On the pool, SELECT resolves [rows, fields] and INSERT resolves [header, undefined] so insertId sits at [0]; on a raw single connection the INSERT resolves to a bare header — that is why const [result] = await db.query(...); result.insertId is wrong on the pool but accidentally right in a probe script, making the bug invisible when tested that way.

HAG-51 report: dashboard schema guards, guest_profiles leg
tableExists guard (rewritten to information_schema)
nodes.rationale: mysql2's query() returns SHOW output as two result sets, so rows.length was always 2 whether the table existed or not — every tableExists call went permanently true; the fix queries information_schema.tables with a bound parameter, keeping the same name and signature.

nodes.label: columnExists guard (rewritten to information_schema)
nodes.rationale: Same two-result-set SHOW COLUMNS defect as tableExists: the guard returned true even when the column was missing; now uses information_schema.columns.

nodes.label: detectDateColumn guard (one query, Set membership)
nodes.rationale: With SHOW probes it unconditionally returned the first candidate (created_at) and threw ER_NO_SUCH_TABLE on a missing table; the fix does one information_schema query and Set membership, still falling back to null when nothing matches.

nodes.label: guests → bookings leg fix (hotel booking check-in source)
nodes.rationale: guest_profiles is an identity table with no check_in/check_in_date/booking_id columns, so renaming the leg to it as dispatched would throw ER_BAD_FIELD_ERROR once the guard became honest; bookings is the correct source (has check_in, already feeds leg 3, and room_tariff.booking_id joins to it) — the legacy false-positive guard had been hiding the fatal rename.

nodes.label: room_tariff table (0 rows, why totalRevenueGenerated < todayRevenue)
guest_profiles table (71 identity rows, no booking dates)
HAG-52 report: banquet INSERT arity mismatch
banquetBookingsController.js (33-column INSERT fixed at :394)
nodes.rationale: The INSERT listed 33 columns but supplied 32 ? placeholders against 33 bind values, so MySQL rejected every booking create with ER_WRONG_VALUE_COUNT_ON_ROW and silently dropped created_by; the fix adds the one missing placeholder, and every other INSERT/UPDATE in the banquet files was audited and is arithmetically consistent.

nodes.label: checkBookingOverlap guard (hall time-slot conflict, lines 326-337)
nodes.rationale: The overlap guard correctly uses the mysql2 tuple contract (const [hallRows] = await db.query(...) then hallRows.length); a 409 on a first probe attempt was caused by the probe's own row, not a defect.
